decks.module: Who needs a Texas license and the learner license

cards.front: Who must hold a Texas license, and how do nonresidents and military drivers fit in?
cards.back: Texas licenses cover residents, ninety-day new residents, non-farm commercial-free machines, sixteen-plus nonresidents for Class C or M, eighteen-plus nonresidents for anything with home reciprocity, and military drivers on home licenses with Texas cards surviving service plus ninety days.

cards.front: How does the new-resident license clock differ from the rule for service members?
cards.back: New residents face a ninety-day clock to qualify for a Texas license, while service members keep an existing Texas card valid through duty plus ninety days after.
cards.memory_hook: newcomers ninety days, service plus ninety

cards.front: Who may ride with a learner driver, who may apply, and what do learner cards cost?
cards.back: Learner driving needs a sober watchful companion twenty-one plus with a year of experience, applicants run fifteen to eighteen with classroom education and exams passed, cards cost sixteen dollars total to age eighteen, practicing adults pay thirty-three dollars total for eight restricted years, and all prior cards surrender first.

cards.front: How does the learner card cost compare with a practicing adult's license cost?
cards.back: A learner card costs sixteen dollars total and ends at eighteen, while a practicing adult pays thirty-three dollars total for eight restricted years.

cards.front: What must an under-eighteen first-time applicant bring from school, and how fresh must it be?
cards.back: Under-eighteen first-timers file a school VOE proving a diploma, eighty prior-term days, or forty-five equivalency-prep days, fresh within thirty days in session or ninety in summer.

cards.front: How long does a school VOE stay valid during the school year versus over summer?
cards.back: A school VOE stays fresh thirty days in session but ninety days across summer.

cards.front: When can a fifteen to eighteen year old get a hardship license, and what does the graduated system require?
cards.back: Hardship licenses aid fifteen- to eighteen-year-olds via in-person adult petitions, full education and exams, and approval only for money crisis, family emergency, vocational need, or court order, inside a graduated system forcing driving exams on all newcomers, six learner months stretched by suspensions, and no Phase One wait for Class M.

cards.front: How is hardship approval different from finishing graduated Phase One?
cards.back: Hardship approval turns on proven need and narrow grounds, while graduated Phase One turns on a six-month learner hold that suspensions stretch.

cards.front: What limits apply to a driver in Phase Two of graduated licensing?
cards.back: Phase Two caps young non-family passengers at one, bans midnight-to-five driving outside work, school, or emergency, and forbids under-eighteen wireless use beyond emergencies.

cards.front: What are the two separate Phase Two limits on riders and night driving?
cards.back: Phase Two caps young non-family riders at one and separately bans midnight-to-five driving outside work, school, or emergency.

cards.front: Who receives a PROVISIONAL card, how are out-of-state teens placed, and how long does an adult license last?
cards.back: PROVISIONAL cards run sixteen to eighteen after education, exams, and six learner months, out-of-state teens sort into Phase One or Two by credential, under-twenty-one cards read UNDER twenty-one, adult licenses run eight years for thirty-three dollars total with shorter special terms, and eight commercial-exempt vehicle types still need Class A or B.

cards.front: How does a PROVISIONAL marking differ from an UNDER twenty-one marking?
cards.back: PROVISIONAL marks sixteen- to eighteen-year-old license holders, while UNDER twenty-one marks every card issued before twenty-one.

cards.front: What vehicles do Class A and Class B licenses cover, and what do they cost?
cards.back: Class A spans B and C vehicles plus heavy combinations towing over ten thousand pounds and Class B spans C vehicles plus heavy singles towing ten thousand or twenty-thousand-pound farm trailers, neither touching motorcycles, each thirty-three dollars total for eight adult years with education through twenty-four or sixteen dollars total at seventeen with education.

cards.front: How is the weight test for Class A different from the one for Class B?
cards.back: Class A combinations are judged by combined weight with heavy towed weight, while Class B singles are judged by single-vehicle weight with lighter towing caps.

cards.front: What does a Class C license cover, what does it cost, and what must come before Class M?
cards.back: Class C spans lighter vehicles, small trailers, and certified three-wheel autocycles but never motorcycles at thirty-three dollars total adult, sixteen dollars total at sixteen with education, or six dollars total at fifteen with hardship, while Class M first demands a passed state motorcycle course with under-eighteen entrants showing classroom education plus a learner license or valid Class C.

cards.front: What are the three price paths for a Class C license?
cards.back: Class C prices split three ways by path, thirty-three dollars total as an adult, sixteen dollars total at sixteen with education, or six dollars total at fifteen with hardship.

cards.front: At what age does motorcycle licensing open, and what does it cost?
cards.back: Motorcycle licensing opens at sixteen after thirty-two plus sixteen hours or fifteen for small bikes via hardship or courses, charging thirty-three dollars total adult, sixteen dollars total young, sixteen to append, and twelve extra at renewal, with sixty-percent-plus disabled veterans skipping fees outside commercial and registrant cases.

cards.front: How does the fee to append Class M differ from the fee when renewing it?
cards.back: Appending M to a live license costs sixteen dollars total, while renewing M adds twelve dollars total on top of renewal.

decks.module: ID cards, donor choices and application proof

cards.front: Who can get a Texas ID card, what does it cost, and what can go on its back?
cards.back: ID cards issue at any age, orient vertical under twenty-one, cost sixteen dollars total for six years through fifty-nine or six dollars total later, and backs allow two emergency contacts with allergy drugs handwritten since DPS prints no medical facts.

cards.front: What does the donor heart on a card mean, and what other choices can applicants make?
cards.back: Donor cards show a heart plus donor as conclusive consent, applicants may fund blindness care, Donate Life, veterans, evidence testing, or youth fees, filing happens in person with voter offers from seventeen years ten months, and men eighteen to twenty-five join selective service automatically.

cards.front: How is the donor heart on the card different from the contribution checkboxes?
cards.back: The donor heart on the card front is binding consent for gifts, while the five contribution checkboxes are optional donations.

cards.front: What must every applicant prove, and what stays on the permanent driving record?
cards.back: Filers prove identity, Social Security, prints, medical fitness, and lawful presence while surrendering foreign licenses, every exam, conviction, and crash persists on the permanent record, and original filers insure each owned vehicle to Texas minimums or swear none qualifies.

cards.front: What must a new applicant finish before taking exams?
cards.back: New residents register all owned vehicles, fees with a one-dollar admin charge precede exams with none by mail, under-twenty-five drivers finish education, everyone finishes Impact Texas Drivers pre-exam, and under-eighteen filings carry a guardian oath signature cancellable before eighteen.

cards.front: What happens after you fail or pass an exam, and what score passes a knowledge exam?
cards.back: Failures park applications ninety days, valid-license adults skip exams, passers earn forty-five-day temporary cards, knowledge exams span Class C originals, waivable Class M, and Class A and B rules with seventy percent passing all, and vision checks can mandate lenses or doctor visits.

cards.front: How does a failed exam outcome differ from a passed exam outcome?
cards.back: Exam failure parks an application ninety days, while exam success earns a forty-five-day temporary card.

cards.front: What passing mark do the Class C, Class M, and Class A and B knowledge exams share?
cards.back: Class C, Class M, and Class A and B exams each test different drivers, yet every one passes at seventy percent or better.

cards.front: When do you take the driving exam, what does it cost, and what makes you fail it?
cards.back: Driving exams follow passed exams and proven insurance in class-matched vehicles, excuse nobody under eighteen, run at offices and schools, skip learners, cost ten dollars to upgrade or fifteen to append M, and fail lawbreakers, the disobedient, the dangerous, and anyone beyond thirty lost points.

cards.front: What are the upgrade fee, the append Class M fee, and the lost-points limit on an exam?
cards.back: Stepping up a class or shedding restrictions costs ten dollars, appending Class M costs fifteen dollars, and any exam fails past thirty lost points.

cards.front: What does the examiner grade on the driving exam, and what equipment rules apply?
cards.back: Grading covers control, observation, positioning, signaling, parking, quick stops, backing, signs, signals, clutch, intersections, turns, right-of-way, following, passing, lanes, and posture, allowing cameras while banning automated parking.

decks.module: Carrying, changing and renewing a license

cards.front: What happens after you pass, and what are the penalties for driving unlicensed?
cards.back: Failed exams reschedule, passers carry the license for officers and crash counterparts, unlicensed fines run two hundred dollars first and twenty-five to two hundred second within a year or Class A jail for deadly uninsured crashes, and restrictions change at any office.

cards.front: How do the penalties for driving unlicensed rise from a first offense onward?
cards.back: Unlicensed fines rise from two hundred dollars first to a twenty-five-to-two-hundred-dollar band on a second within a year, then leap to Class A jail for deadly uninsured crashes.

cards.front: What do duplicates and address changes cost, and how fast must you report a move?
cards.back: Duplicates and address moves cost eleven dollars total with thirty-day reporting, ten dollars by mail, other changes in person, no remote service for special licenses, and renewal notices stay pure courtesy.

cards.front: How often do you renew, when must you appear in person, and who may not renew remotely?
cards.back: Renewal runs eight years with office visits each sixteen for vision and biometrics, remote service bars troubled, commercial, restricted, registrant, older, undocumented, and non-citizen filers, medical answers may reach the board, service families renew exam-free within ninety days of discharge, and out-of-state Texans mail fees and vision results to the printed date or ninety days after return.

cards.front: How does the renewal cycle differ from the in-person visit cycle?
cards.back: Licenses renew every eight years, yet every driver still appears in person at least each sixteen years for vision and biometrics.

cards.front: What does reinstatement cost, and which convictions open a revocation?
cards.back: Reinstatement costs one hundred dollars standard or one hundred twenty-five for revocations with possible SR-twenty-two, opening on intoxicated-driving, drug, and assault convictions.

cards.front: Which acts lead to an automatic license suspension?
cards.back: Automatic suspension adds aid failures, deadly crashes, felonies, bus repeats, boating intoxication, evading, invalid driving, card fraud, graffiti, fake plates, false records, and racing.

cards.front: What conviction patterns lead to a hearing suspension, and what suspends under-twenty-one drivers automatically?
cards.back: Hearings suspend for bad patterns of four convictions in twelve months or seven in twenty-four plus exam and probation failures, and under-twenty-one drivers fall automatically for alcohol, tobacco-class, drug, and Chapter four eighty-one offenses.

cards.front: How many convictions over which periods trigger a hearing review?
cards.back: Hearing review follows four convictions in twelve months but needs seven in twenty-four.

cards.front: When are minors suspended, when is a license revoked for intoxication, and when is it cancelled?
cards.back: Minors face hearing suspension for orders, fines, repeat tickets, or delinquency, intoxication revocation costs one hundred twenty-five dollars back and strikes at point zero eight adult, any refusal, and any under-twenty-one detection, and cancellation follows foreign actions, lost approval, gaps, or lies.

cards.front: How does the alcohol limit for revocation differ for adults and drivers under twenty-one?
cards.back: Revocation starts at point zero eight for twenty-one-plus drivers but at any detectable alcohol under twenty-one.
cards.memory_hook: adults point zero eight, minors any

cards.front: Which court orders compel action on a driver license?
cards.back: Court orders compel action for child support, interlock, overpayments, incapacity, dependency, or lapsed annual renewal.

decks.module: Denial, Zero Tolerance and occupational licenses

cards.front: On what grounds is a license denied, and how are drivers punished for driving while invalid?
cards.back: Denials track live disqualifications, unsafe conditions, theft, mischief, minor alcohol supply, support debt, unpaid fees, missed court, and drugs, while invalid driving scales from Class C fines through Class B jail to Class A jail with extensions, and skipped traffic court can block renewal.

cards.front: What does Zero Tolerance ban, and how do penalties grow with repeat offenses?
cards.back: Zero Tolerance bans all minor alcohol contact, fining first offenses up to five hundred dollars with eight to twelve service hours, courses, and thirty suspended days, seconds with twenty to forty hours and sixty days, thirds at seventeen to twenty reaching Class B and one hundred eighty days without deferred disposition, and under-seventeen thirds at sixty days or juvenile court.

cards.front: How do Zero Tolerance suspension lengths climb across offenses?
cards.back: Zero Tolerance suspensions climb thirty, sixty, then one hundred eighty days across offenses, with the oldest teens reaching Class B and denied deferral.

cards.front: What can happen to someone who supplies alcohol to a minor?
cards.back: Supplying alcohol to a minor risks four thousand dollars, a year in jail, or both.

cards.front: How does an occupational license work, and what does it cost?
cards.back: Court-proved essential need buys occupational licenses at ten dollars yearly or twenty for two, the order alone covering forty-five processing days before both order and certified copy ride along, never for commercial rigs.

recaps.module: Who needs a Texas license and the learner license

recap_hooks.text: Residents and newcomers need a Texas license, with ninety days to qualify after moving in.
Learners drive with a sober companion at least twenty-one with a year of experience.
Under-eighteen first-timers bring a fresh school VOE form.
Hardship licenses need proven need on narrow grounds.
Phase Two allows one young non-family rider and no midnight-to-five driving except for work, school, or emergency.
PROVISIONAL marks teen license holders; UNDER twenty-one marks young cards.
Class A covers heavy combinations and Class B heavy single vehicles.
Class C covers lighter vehicles but never motorcycles.
Motorcycle licensing opens at sixteen after the required course.

recaps.module: ID cards, donor choices and application proof

recap_hooks.text: ID cards issue at any age and can list emergency contacts.
The donor heart is binding consent; contributions are optional.
Applicants prove identity and insure their vehicles, then finish Impact Texas Drivers before exams.
A failed exam parks the application; a passed exam earns a temporary card.
Every knowledge exam passes at seventy percent or better.
The driving exam needs insurance and a class-matched vehicle and grades control, observation, and signaling.

recaps.module: Carrying, changing and renewing a license

recap_hooks.text: Carry your license; unlicensed driving fines rise with repeat offenses.
Report an address move within thirty days.
Renew every eight years and appear in person at least every sixteen.
Some acts suspend a license automatically; patterns of convictions lead to a hearing.
Adults are revoked at point zero eight; drivers under twenty-one at any detectable alcohol.
Reinstatement has a fee, and court orders can compel license action.

recaps.module: Denial, Zero Tolerance and occupational licenses

recap_hooks.text: Licenses can be denied, and driving while invalid brings rising penalties.
Zero Tolerance bans all minor alcohol contact, with suspensions climbing on repeat offenses.
Supplying alcohol to a minor risks a large fine and jail; occupational licenses need court-proved essential need.
